bridge-provider.title: Implement the Provider Message Adapter
bridge-provider.action: Connect the raw loop to one pinned provider SDK using offline response fixtures before enabling paid requests.
bridge-provider.evidence: A tested adapter preserves tool IDs, content blocks, stop reasons, and usage without making live calls.
objectives: Translate the raw harness message contract into a provider request.
Preserve tool-call/result semantics and account for every outbound request.
before: The raw `FakeModel` loop, strict tool dispatcher, shared evaluator, and verified execution boundary.
Use one provider with a documented tool interface; the worked reference is the official Anthropic Python SDK. An alternative provider needs equivalent tests.
bridge-provider.explanation: An SDK transports requests; your harness still owns the loop. A real response may contain text, multiple tool calls, provider-specific continuation data, a stop reason, and usage fields. Reducing that response to one string loses information needed by the next turn. Keep a provider representation alongside your normalized records, validate proposed actions, and return each result using the correct call ID. Today builds the adapter against offline fixtures. The next budget lesson authorizes the first small live call only after reservation tests pass.

plan.title: Build
plan.text: Create `harness/provider.py` behind the `FakeModel` interface. Serialize task, system instructions, tool schema, and prior messages for one chosen model. Preserve complete provider-required response blocks and normalize tool IDs, stop reason, model/request identifiers, and available usage. Configure explicit timeouts and disable automatic SDK retries so the harness can count attempts. Start with one tool call per response if supported; otherwise handle all calls sequentially and return every result, or reject an unsupported multi-call response before any tool executes. Use synthetic provider fixtures for final text, one tool call, two tool calls, and output-limit termination. Treat truncated output as a distinct bounded outcome. Keep the API key outside logs and task containers; do not make live requests today.

plan.title: Verify and save
plan.text: Run the offline adapter cases through the existing loop. Save a sanitized request/response/tool-result example and SDK/model configuration. Confirm the HTTP spy records no network calls in this test mode.

checks: Final text, one-tool, multi-tool, and truncated-response cases have explicit outcomes.

selfCheck.question: Why not keep only the first text field of a provider response?
selfCheck.answer: The response may include tool calls and provider-required continuation blocks. Dropping them breaks message causality and can make the next request invalid; a text string is not the full protocol state.

bridge-provider.pitfall: Do not treat an output-length stop as successful task completion, or silently execute only the first call in a multi-call response.
